⚠️: First build. The corpus is a single closed text, so unlike German and Arabic these counts are not a sample of a language — they describe the Qur'an exactly.

method.frequency: One pass over the full mushaf: 6,348 stored verses (6,236 canonical + 112 basmala entries), 77,878 word tokens, 14,811 distinct surface forms, summed onto lemmas. --min-count 1 because a curated text has no OCR tail to filter — a word occurring once in the Qur'an is a real word. The default floor of 20, tuned for Leipzig's ~10M tokens, deleted 97% of the vocabulary and produced a 404-entry list.
method.lemmatizer: Wikidata Lexemes (CC0), Arabic Q13955. The table is built against the Leipzig Arabic corpora AND the Qur'an together — see sources.json wikidata-lexemes-ar. Ranking uses Qur'anic counts only.
method.orthography: Uthmani → modern rewrites, each conditional on resolving to a known word: ٱ→ا, ءا→آ, ىء→يء, final ى→ي. Unconditional rules corrupt the head of the list (على→علي). 2,689 of 14,811 forms differ from their mushaf spelling; out/uthmani.tsv preserves it.

lexiconCoverage.note: Share of Qur'anic TOKENS that the CC0 Wikidata lexicon recognises, at each stage of normalization. Measured 2026-07-30.

coverage.note: ⚠️ NOT MEASURED. No held-out evaluation exists — and for a single closed text the usual notion of held-out coverage does not straightforwardly apply. Do not cite a figure.
